abstract.para: A tailoring file adapts a profile to local requirements without changing the content of the &ssg;. The autotailor command creates tailoring files, and oscap uses them for scans and remediation.

section.title: Tailoring files
section.para: A tailoring file defines a custom profile that extends a base profile. The custom profile can add or remove rules and override the values of variables.

To create tailoring files on &productnameshort; 16, use autotailor from the openscap-utils package. SCAP Workbench and ssg-apply, which earlier &sle; versions provide for tailoring, are not available for &productnameshort; 16. For more information about installing the package, see .

section.title: Creating and using a tailoring file
section.para: The following procedure creates a custom profile from the Health Insurance Portability and Accountability Act (HIPAA) profile. The custom profile adds the rule sshd_limit_user_access, which limits SSH access for users.

To check that the tailoring file contains the custom profile, run the following command:
step.screen: &prompt.user;oscap info /tmp/ssg-sle16-ds-tailoring.xml Document type: XCCDF Tailoring Imported: 2026-10-16T12:39:16 Benchmark Hint: file:///usr/share/xml/scap/ssg/content/ssg-sle16-ds.xml Profiles: Title: HIPAA (customized) Id: xccdf_org.ssgproject.content_profile_hipaa_customized

step.para: Compared to a scan with the HIPAA profile, the output contains one additional rule:
step.screen: Title Limit Users' SSH Access Rule xccdf_org.ssgproject.content_rule_sshd_limit_user_access Ident CCE-96002-1 Result fail

section.para: To override the value of a variable, use the --var-value option of autotailor. For example, --var-value var_password_pam_minlen=12 changes the required minimum password length to 12 characters. The rule accounts_password_pam_minlen then checks for this value.

section.title: Remediating with a tailoring file
section.para: With the --remediate option, oscap remediates each rule that fails during the scan.

warning.title: Changes to the running system
warning.para: Remediation changes the configuration of the running system immediately. For example, remediating the complete HIPAA profile installs the cronie and postfix packages, disables root login over SSH and blocks the usb-storage kernel module.
Test the remediation on a non-production system before you apply it to a production system.

section.para: To remediate only one rule of the custom profile, add the --rule option, as in .

example.title: Remediating a single rule
example.screen:
&prompt.sudo;oscap xccdf eval --remediate \ --profile xccdf_org.ssgproject.content_profile_hipaa_customized \ --tailoring-file /tmp/ssg-sle16-ds-tailoring.xml \ --rule xccdf_org.ssgproject.content_rule_sysctl_kernel_randomize_va_space \ --results /tmp/results-remediated.xml \ /usr/share/xml/scap/ssg/content/ssg-sle16-ds.xml --- Starting Evaluation ---
Title Enable Randomized Layout of Virtual Address Space Rule xccdf_org.ssgproject.content_rule_sysctl_kernel_randomize_va_space Ident CCE-96568-1 Result fail
--- Starting Remediation ---
Title Enable Randomized Layout of Virtual Address Space Rule xccdf_org.ssgproject.content_rule_sysctl_kernel_randomize_va_space Ident CCE-96568-1 Result fixed

section.para: The result fixed shows that the remediation was successful. In this example, oscap creates the file /etc/sysctl.d/kernel_randomize_va_space.conf with the setting kernel.randomize_va_space = 2.
